# **Part 2: Elevator Pitch of Project/Product**

*Remember to address the questions in the Phase 1 Requirements document.*

1. What are you building?  
2. Why is this data-driven app important?  
3. What pain points from existing solutions do you hope to address by collecting, storing, and/or analyzing data?   
4. What are the major user types/categories/personas that you are building the app for?   
5. Tease the reader with two to three key features your app will provide. 

There are far too many promising high school athletes who are overlooked or not even noticed by college recruiters. This waste of talent is the unfortunate product of young athletes not knowing how to best market themselves. We are committed to sharing athletic talent with the world through the development of TalentScout.   
TalentScout is a bidirectional recruiting platform for athletes and recruiters. Athletes can professionally share their accomplishments through uploading short sport highlight clips, while recruiters will be able to scroll through the clips to discover promising talent. These scouts will be able to input their roster needs so that only the clips of the most relevant athletes are shown. Furthermore, TalentScout features profile pages to hold all athletes’ posts, a feed page to see the clips, and the tailored coach’s feed serving as the key differentiator to actually make these connections happen. Although TalentScount will not be the first app to step onto the field, we are confident that we will fill a gap in the market by being a bidirectional recruiting platform.  

# **Part 3: User Personas**

## **Persona 1:** High School Athlete (BETHANY)

**What’s Their Story**:  
Bethany is a Sophomore at North Mist High School. She’s been obsessed with Track & Field ever since she first heard about it in 5th grade. She joined the club team in middle school and was the first high school freshman to make varsity, to the credit of her 100m hurdle time.  
Bethany’s fast, but her school is in a part of the state where college scouts rarely visit, and neither of her parents were college athletes so no one she knows really gets how recruiting actually works. She’s watched teammates with worse times get looks simply because they could afford the $2,000 recruiting service or had a club coach with connections.

### User Stories for Persona 1:

1.  As a student athlete, Bethany wants to be able to upload her PRs, events, height, GPA, and graduation year to show recruiters who she is and what she’s capable of.  
2.  As a student athlete, Bethany wants to update her PR times, GPA, and other metrics as they change each season and semester to show recruiters a current accurate reflection of herself.  
3.  As a student athlete, Bethany wants to upload highlight clips of her races to her profile to entice recruiters with her content and skill.  
4.  As a student athlete, Bethany wants to see a list of college programs whose roster needs match her events, metrics, and academics to show her how she should be marketing herself via the platform and to see what scouts are actually looking for.  
5.  As a student athlete, Bethany wants a viewing feature that shows which coaches have viewed her profile and clips so she can see who’s interested in her profile and reach out to the coach.  
6.  As a student athlete, Bethany wants to mark her profile with a status like committed / open to recruitment / inactive so recruiters know what this athlete is looking for and how to approach them.

## **Persona 2:** College Recruiters (KEVIN)

**What’s Their Story**?  
Kevin is a middle-aged college football recruiter from South Lake University. He is currently looking for three promising athletes to add to his team but he has been dissatisfied with the recruiting services he has found so far as they have been too difficult for him to navigate. Kevin has tried touring other schools to look for talent on the ground but that is very time consuming and South Lake recently cut his travel funds. 

### *User Stories for Persona 2:*

1. As a recruiter, Kevin wants to be able to scroll through sports clips  
2. As a recruiter, Kevin should be able to upload his roster to see more relevant clips  
3. As a recruiter, Kevin wants to be able to see more information about the athletes in clips he sees  
4. As a recruiter, Kevin needs to be able to query for athletes that meet specific metrics  
5. As a recruiter, Kevin should be able to see athletes who are interested in his roster  
6. As a recruiter, Kevin would like to be able to see the students who have viewed and interacted with his profile

## **Persona 3:** Administrator (JONATHAN)

**What’s their Story**:  
	Jonathan is a platform administrator working at TalentScout. Jonathan was brought on board to moderate platform content and manage account support. He works remotely and supervises content, occasionally answering the phone for a support ticket. 

### *User Stories for Persona 3:*

1. As an administrator, Jonathan can see an unfiltered feed like a college recruiter to scan profiles for content violations  
2. As an administrator, Jonathan can delete posts as necessary for content violations so the platform remains appropriate  
3. As an administrator, Jonathan can view and delete athlete accounts for content violations so the platform remains appropriate  
4. As an administrator, Jonathan can view and delete roster postings by college accounts so the platform does not have false rosters and maintains integrity  
5. As an administrator, Jonathan can delete post comments so the platform remains appropriate  
6. As an administrator, Jonathan can create announcements on the website so TalentScout can effectively communicate with its users

## **Persona 4: Data Analyst (LORI)**

**What’s their Story**: Lori is a master’s data researcher at Sandstone University. She is studying young adult sports and how college athletes’ outcomes differ from their peers not participating in competitive athletics. As part of her research she is gathering data about high school athletes. 

### *User Stories for Persona 4:*

1.  As a Data analyst, Lori can see aggregate tables of data, such as percentages, averages, and counts so she can obtain quantitative metrics.  
2.  As a Data analyst, Lori can filter by different conditions such as gender and sport so she can compare metrics between different groups.   
3.  As a Data analyst, Lori can see individual profiles in an anonymous manner without videos so she can get anecdotes and remove outliers.  
4.  As a Data analyst, Lori can export data (CSV) so she can analyze data further in her preferred application.  
5.  As a Data analyst, Lori can see historical PR data to compare data on different time frames.  
6.  As a Data analyst, Lori can graph data to perform quick, macro analysis

# Queries for User Stories

*For each of your user stories, provide a single SQL SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE statement that would solve the data needs of the user story.  Label each Query with its corresponding User Story Number (e.g., “2.4” for user story 4 of persona \#2, or something similar). Each SQL statement should be written to work with your data model.* 

*The SQL Statements provided should be **formatted appropriately** and in a **fixed-point font** such as Courier or Fira Mono.* 

**STUDENT ATHLETE**  
`1.1)`  
`INSERT INTO athlete (user_id, graduation_year, dob, gender, height_cm,`      
`weight_kg, gpa, recruitment_status)`  
`VALUES (9, 2029, '2011-07-19', 'M', 181, 71, 3.00, 'open');`

`1.2)`  
`UPDATE athlete`  
`SET gpa = 3.91, height_cm = 164, weight_kg = 56`  
`WHERE user_id = 1;`

`1.3)`  
`INSERT INTO clip (user_id, posted_at, caption)`  
`VALUES (1, '2026-08-10', 'Regional 100m hurdles final - new PR');`

`1.4)`  
`SELECT r.team_name, u.name AS university, o.position, o.required_gpa,`  
`o.required_height_cm, o.grad_year`  
`FROM opening o`  
`JOIN roster r ON o.roster_id = r.roster_id`  
	`JOIN recruiter rec ON r.user_id = rec.user_id`  
	`JOIN university u ON rec.university_id = u.university_id`  
`WHERE o.required_gpa <=`   
`(SELECT gpa FROM athlete WHERE user_id = 1)`  
`AND o.required_height_cm <=`   
`(SELECT height_cm FROM athlete WHERE user_id = 1)`  
`AND o.grad_year =`  
`(SELECT graduation_year FROM athlete WHERE user_id = 1);`

`1.5)`  
`SELECT u.first_name, u.last_name, uni.name AS university, rv.view_time`  
`FROM recruiter_view rv`  
`JOIN recruiter rec ON rv.recruiter_id = rec.user_id`  
	`JOIN user u ON rec.user_id = u.user_id`  
	`JOIN university uni ON rec.university_id = uni.university_id`  
`WHERE rv.athlete_id = 1`  
`ORDER BY rv.view_time DESC;`

`1.6)`  
`UPDATE athlete`  
`SET recruitment_status = 'committed'`  
`WHERE user_id = 1;`

**`COLLEGE RECRUITERS`**  
`2.1)`  
`SELECT c.clip_id, c.caption, c.posted_at, c.user_id AS athlete_id`  
`FROM clip c`  
`ORDER BY c.posted_at DESC;`

`2.2)`  
`INSERT INTO roster (user_id, sport_id, division, start_date, end_date,`  
`gender, team_name)`  
`VALUES (2, 1, 'D1', '2026-08-01', '2027-05-31', 'M', 'South Lake Football');`

`2.3)`  
`SELECT a.user_id, u.first_name, u.last_name, a.gpa, a.height_cm,`  
`a.weight_kg, a.graduation_year, a.recruitment_status`  
`FROM clip c`  
`JOIN athlete a ON c.user_id = a.user_id`  
	`JOIN user u ON a.user_id = u.user_id`  
`WHERE c.clip_id = 1;`

`2.4)`  
`SELECT a.user_id, u.first_name, u.last_name, a.gpa, a.height_cm,`  
`a.graduation_year`  
`FROM athlete a`  
`JOIN user u ON a.user_id = u.user_id`  
`WHERE a.gpa >= 3.00`  
`AND a.height_cm >= 140`  
`AND a.graduation_year = 2027;`

`2.5)`  
`SELECT a.user_id, u.first_name, u.last_name, a.gpa, a.height_cm,`  
`rv.view_time`  
`FROM roster_view rv`  
`JOIN roster r ON rv.roster_id = r.roster_id`  
	`JOIN athlete a ON rv.user_id = a.user_id`  
	`JOIN user u ON a.user_id = u.user_id`  
`WHERE r.user_id = 2`  
`ORDER BY rv.view_time DESC;`

`2.6)`  
`SELECT a.user_id, u.first_name, u.last_name, rv.view_time`  
`FROM recruiter_view rv`  
	`JOIN athlete a ON rv.athlete_id = a.user_id`  
	`JOIN user u ON a.user_id = u.user_id`  
`WHERE rv.recruiter_id = 2`  
`ORDER BY rv.view_time DESC;`

**`ADMINISTRATOR`**  
`3.1)`

`ORDER BY c.posted_at DESC;`

`3.2)`

**`DATA ANALYST`**  
`4.1)`  
`SELECT s.name AS sport,`  
`COUNT(*) AS athlete_count,`  
`AVG(a.gpa) AS avg_gpa,`  
`AVG(a.height_cm) AS avg_height_cm,`  
`AVG(a.weight_kg) AS avg_weight_kg`  
`FROM athlete a`  
`JOIN roster_view rv ON a.user_id = rv.user_id`  
`JOIN roster r ON rv.roster_id = r.roster_id`  
`JOIN sport s ON r.sport_id = s.sport_id`  
`GROUP BY s.name;`

`4.2)`  
`SELECT a.gender,`  
	`COUNT(*) AS athlete_count,`  
`AVG(a.gpa) AS avg_gpa,`  
`AVG(a.height_cm) AS avg_height_cm`  
`FROM athlete a`  
`GROUP BY a.gender;`

`4.3`  
`SELECT a.user_id AS anonymous_id, a.gender, a.gpa, a.height_cm,`  
`a.weight_kg, a.graduation_year`  
`FROM athlete a;`

`4.4)`  
`SELECT u.user_id, a.gender, a.gpa, a.height_cm, a.weight_kg, a.graduation_year, a.recruitment_status`  
`FROM athlete a`  
`JOIN user u ON a.user_id = u.user_id;`

`4.5)`  
`SELECT e.name AS event, pr.date,`  
`SEC_TO_TIME(AVG(TIME_TO_SEC(pr.time))) AS avg_time,`  
`COUNT(*) AS record_count`  
`FROM personal_record pr`  
`JOIN event e ON pr.event_id = e.event_id`  
	`GROUP BY e.name, pr.date`  
`ORDER BY e.name, pr.date;`

`4.6)`  
`SELECT a.graduation_year,`  
`COUNT(*) AS athlete_count,`  
`AVG(a.gpa) AS avg_gpa`  
`FROM athlete a`  
`GROUP BY a.graduation_year`  
`ORDER BY a.graduation_year;`

# SQL Code:

Copy and paste your SQL DDL (and any other related SQL) below.  Be sure that you DO NOT paste a screenshot.  All code should be appropriately formatted and presented in a fixed-width font. 

**`DDL:`**  
`DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS talent_scout;`  
`CREATE DATABASE talent_scout;`  
`USE talent_scout;`

`DROP TABLE IF EXISTS user;`  
`CREATE TABLE user`  
`(`  
    `user_id    INT AUTO_INCREMENT,`  
    `first_name VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL,`  
    `last_name  VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL,`  
    `email      VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL UNIQUE,`  
    `phone      CHAR(10),`  
    `PRIMARY KEY (user_id)`  
`);`

`-- Analyst`  
`DROP TABLE IF EXISTS analyst;`  
`CREATE TABLE analyst`  
`(`  
    `user_id INT,`  
    `PRIMARY KEY (user_id),`  
    `FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES user (user_id)`  
        `ON UPDATE CASCADE`  
        `ON DELETE CASCADE`  
`);`

`-- Administrator`  
`DROP TABLE IF EXISTS administrator;`  
`CREATE TABLE administrator`  
`(`  
    `user_id INT,`  
    `PRIMARY KEY (user_id),`  
    `FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES user (user_id)`  
        `ON UPDATE CASCADE`  
        `ON DELETE CASCADE`  
`);`

`DROP TABLE IF EXISTS announcement;`  
`CREATE TABLE announcement`  
`(`  
    `announcement_id INT AUTO_INCREMENT,`  
    `user_id         INT,`  
    `title           TINYTEXT NOT NULL,`  
    `body            MEDIUMTEXT,`  
    `scheduled_start DATETIME NOT NULL,`  
    `scheduled_end   DATETIME NOT NULL,`  
    `PRIMARY KEY (announcement_id),`  
    `FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES administrator (user_id)`  
        `ON UPDATE CASCADE`  
        `ON DELETE SET NULL`  
`);`

`-- Recruiter`  
`DROP TABLE IF EXISTS university;`  
`CREATE TABLE university`  
`(`  
    `university_id INT AUTO_INCREMENT,`  
    `website_url   VARCHAR(80),`  
    `name          VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL UNIQUE,`  
    `PRIMARY KEY (university_id)`  
`);`

`DROP TABLE IF EXISTS recruiter;`  
`CREATE TABLE recruiter`  
`(`  
    `user_id       INT,`  
    `university_id INT,`  
    `PRIMARY KEY (user_id),`  
    `FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES user (user_id)`  
        `ON UPDATE CASCADE`  
        `ON DELETE CASCADE,`  
    `FOREIGN KEY (university_id) REFERENCES university (university_id)`  
        `ON UPDATE CASCADE`  
        `ON DELETE RESTRICT`  
`);`

`DROP TABLE IF EXISTS sport;`  
`CREATE TABLE sport`  
`(`  
    `sport_id INT AUTO_INCREMENT,`  
    `name     VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL UNIQUE,`  
    `PRIMARY KEY (sport_id)`  
`);`

`DROP TABLE IF EXISTS roster;`  
`CREATE TABLE roster`  
`(`  
    `roster_id  INT AUTO_INCREMENT,`  
    `user_id    INT,`  
    `sport_id   INT,`  
    `division   TINYTEXT,`  
    `start_date DATE        NOT NULL,`  
    `end_date   DATE        NOT NULL,`  
    `gender     CHAR(1)     NOT NULL,`  
    `team_name  VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL,`  
    `PRIMARY KEY (roster_id),`  
    `FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES recruiter (user_id)`  
        `ON UPDATE CASCADE`  
        `ON DELETE CASCADE,`  
    `FOREIGN KEY (sport_id) REFERENCES sport (sport_id)`  
        `ON UPDATE CASCADE`  
        `ON DELETE RESTRICT`  
`);`

`DROP TABLE IF EXISTS opening;`  
`CREATE TABLE opening`  
`(`  
    `opening_number     INT,`  
    `roster_id          INT,`  
    `required_gpa       DECIMAL(3, 2),`  
    `required_height_cm INT,`  
    `position           VARCHAR(20),`  
    `grad_year          YEAR,`  
    `PRIMARY KEY (opening_number, roster_id),`  
    `FOREIGN KEY (roster_id) REFERENCES roster (roster_id)`  
        `ON UPDATE CASCADE`  
        `ON DELETE CASCADE`  
`);`

`-- Athlete`  
`DROP TABLE IF EXISTS athlete;`  
`CREATE TABLE athlete`  
`(`  
    `user_id            INT,`  
    `graduation_year    YEAR          NOT NULL,`  
    `dob                DATE          NOT NULL,`  
    `gender             CHAR(1)       NOT NULL,`  
    `height_cm          INT           NOT NULL,`  
    `weight_kg          INT           NOT NULL,`  
    `gpa                DECIMAL(3, 2) NOT NULL,`  
    `recruitment_status VARCHAR(10),`  
    `PRIMARY KEY (user_id),`  
    `FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES user (user_id)`  
        `ON UPDATE CASCADE`  
        `ON DELETE CASCADE`  
`);`

`DROP TABLE IF EXISTS event;`  
`CREATE TABLE event`  
`(`  
    `event_id INT AUTO_INCREMENT,`  
    `name     VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL UNIQUE,`  
    `PRIMARY KEY (event_id)`  
`);`

`DROP TABLE IF EXISTS personal_record;`  
`CREATE TABLE personal_record`  
`(`  
    `user_id  INT,`  
    `date     DATE,`  
    `event_id INT,`  
    `time     TIME(2),`  
    `score    DOUBLE,`  
    `PRIMARY KEY (user_id, date, event_id),`  
    `FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES athlete (user_id)`  
        `ON UPDATE CASCADE`  
        `ON DELETE CASCADE,`  
    `FOREIGN KEY (event_id) REFERENCES event (event_id)`  
        `ON UPDATE CASCADE`  
        `ON DELETE RESTRICT`  
`);`

`DROP TABLE IF EXISTS clip;`  
`CREATE TABLE clip`  
`(`  
    `clip_id   INT AUTO_INCREMENT,`  
    `user_id   INT,`  
    `posted_at DATE     NOT NULL,`  
    `caption   TINYTEXT NOT NULL,`  
    `PRIMARY KEY (clip_id),`  
    `FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES athlete (user_id)`  
        `ON UPDATE CASCADE`  
        `ON DELETE CASCADE`  
`);`

`DROP TABLE IF EXISTS comment;`  
`CREATE TABLE comment`  
`(`  
    `comment_id INT AUTO_INCREMENT,`  
    `clip_id    INT,`  
    `user_id    INT,`  
    `posted_at  DATE     NOT NULL,`  
    `content    TINYTEXT NOT NULL,`  
    `PRIMARY KEY (comment_id),`  
    `FOREIGN KEY (clip_id) REFERENCES clip (clip_id)`  
        `ON UPDATE CASCADE`  
        `ON DELETE CASCADE,`  
    `FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES user (user_id)`  
        `ON UPDATE CASCADE`  
        `ON DELETE SET NULL`  
`);`

`-- View`  
`DROP TABLE IF EXISTS roster_view;`  
`CREATE TABLE roster_view`  
`(`  
    `user_id   INT,`  
    `roster_id INT,`  
    `view_time DATETIME NOT NULL,`  
    `PRIMARY KEY (user_id, roster_id),`  
    `FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES athlete (user_id)`  
        `ON UPDATE CASCADE`  
        `ON DELETE CASCADE,`  
    `FOREIGN KEY (roster_id) REFERENCES roster (roster_id)`  
        `ON UPDATE CASCADE`  
        `ON DELETE CASCADE`  
`);`

`DROP TABLE IF EXISTS recruiter_view;`  
`CREATE TABLE recruiter_view`  
`(`  
    `athlete_id   INT,`  
    `recruiter_id INT,`  
    `view_time    DATETIME NOT NULL,`  
    `PRIMARY KEY (athlete_id, recruiter_id),`  
    `FOREIGN KEY (athlete_id) REFERENCES athlete (user_id)`  
        `ON UPDATE CASCADE`  
        `ON DELETE CASCADE,`  
    `FOREIGN KEY (recruiter_id) REFERENCES recruiter (user_id)`  
        `ON UPDATE CASCADE`  
        `ON DELETE CASCADE`  
`);`

| `RESOURCES` | `GET` | `POST` | `PUT` | `DELETE` |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **`/athlete`** | `2.4 - Query athletes that fit certain criteria 4.1 - Data analysts can get overall data on athletes 4.2 - Same thing, overall data with filters 4.3 - But anonymous 4.4 - But there’s an export button 4.6 - Access data to make graphs` | `1.1 - Add data to athlete profile` |  |  |
| **`/athlete /<athlete_id>`** | `2.3 - Recruiters can view detailed info about athletes` |  | `1.2 - Update data on athlete profile 1.6 - Can change profile status` | `3.3 - Delete athletes` |
| **`/announcement`** | `3.6 - Everyone can get announcements` | `3.6 - Create announcements for everyone to see` |  |  |
| **`/clip`** | `2.1 - Feed of clips 3.1 - Unfiltered feed of clips` | `1.3 - Upload clips to show off highlights` |  |  |
| **`/roster`** | `1.4 - Return rosters that are looking for someone with the athlete's metrics` | `2.2 - Upload roster to see more relevant clips` |  |  |
| **`/recruiter_view /<athlete_id>`** | `1.5 - Return info of recruiters that viewed the athlete's profile` | `1.5 - Mark a view of an athlete by a recruiter`  |  |  |
| **`/roster_view /<roster_id>`** | `2.5 - See who viewed the recruiter's specific roster` | `2.5 - Mark a view of a roster by an athlete` |  |  |
| **`/clip/<clip_id>`** | `Gets a clip and all of its comments` |  |  | `3.2 - Delete posts` |
| **`/roster /<roster_id>`** |  |  |  | `3.4 - Delete rosters to maintain integrity` |
| **`/recruiter /<id>`** | `1.5 - Athletes can view details about coaches who view them` |  |  | `3.4 - Delete recruiters`  |
| **`/comment /<comment_id>`** |  |  |  | `3.5 - Delete comments for appropriate content` |
| **`/Personal_Record`** | `4.5 - Compare historical data` |  |  |  |
| **`/opening`** | `Gets list of all openings` | `Create an opening for a roster` |  |  |
| **`/comment`** |  | `Create a comment` |  |  |
